name: Dana Kowalczyk
equipment: Tactical vest (her own plate carrier with soft armour panels, from a range day she never got to)
Keys to a 2014 Chevy Silverado, half a tank, parked on Third Street
Missouri National Guard ID (Sergeant, 1138th Engineer Company, on leave)
features: Human Versatility (Human: +1 to all ability scores)
Combat Training: Marksman (+2 to ranged attack rolls; already included in her ranged attack bonuses)
Adrenaline (bonus action: regain 1d10 + 1 hit points, once per short or long rest)
Proficiencies (Melee, Sidearms, Longarms, Automatics, Explosives; Light, Medium and Heavy armor)
Chain of Command (Veteran feature: soldiers, police and veterans recognise her rank and bearing, and will share information, shelter or a ride with her when it does not put them at risk)

personality.traits: I count rounds out loud under my breath, every shot, mine and everybody else's. I make a plan, tell it in one sentence, and then do it. I am at my calmest when everyone else is at their worst.
personality.ideals: Discipline keeps people alive. Not courage, not luck — the boring stuff: watch rotations, water discipline, knowing exactly how many rounds you have left.
personality.bonds: My unit was called up to the Route 9 bridge without me, because I was on leave. They are somewhere out there. I am going to find out where.
personality.flaws: I do not trust anybody who cannot follow a simple instruction, and I let them know it. I would rather do a job myself than watch someone do it badly.

appearance: Thirty-one, five foot six, compact and square-shouldered, with dark blonde hair scraped back under a faded Cardinals cap and a sunburn line at the collar. Wears jeans, work boots and a grey Army PT T-shirt under a plate carrier she has adjusted so often the straps are frayed. Squints at everything, as if estimating the range.
backstory: Dana Kowalczyk grew up in Corbin's Ferry, enlisted at eighteen, did one tour in Afghanistan as a combat engineer and came home to drive a concrete truck for Haskett Ready-Mix and serve one weekend a month as a sergeant in the Missouri National Guard. She was on leave for Ferry Days, with her rifle and her vest in the truck after a morning at the county range, and was sitting on her tailgate eating a funnel cake when the Ruth Ellen ran aground. On Sunday, when the Guard came to the bridge, it was her own battalion — but not her company, and nobody there had orders to take her back. She has not stopped thinking about that.
